title: India-Pakistan Cricket Final and Hockey Semi-Final Set Asian Games Viewership Records
excerpt: The Olympic Council of Asia said Sunday that the two India-Pakistan clashes at Aichi-Nagoya drew the biggest broadcast audience in Asian Games history — and India won both matches before taking gold in each sport.
body:
• The Olympic Council of Asia said on Sunday that the men's cricket final and hockey semifinal between India and Pakistan at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games were the most-viewed matches in the event's history.
  • India beat Pakistan 4-3 in a last-minute hockey semifinal thriller on Thursday, then defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the cricket final on Saturday — and went on to win gold in both events.
  • No viewership figures were disclosed: OCA Coordination Committee president Tayyab Ikram said the Games had the biggest broadcast audience ever but did not say which of the two matches drew the larger audience.
  • The Aichi-Nagoya Games also produced 212 Asian Games records, 54 world records, 89 Asian records and 11 junior world records, the OCA said.

NAGOYA: The India-Pakistan rivalry has written another chapter into Asian Games history. The Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) said on Sunday that the men's cricket final and men's hockey semifinal between the two arch-rivals at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Games were the most-viewed matches in the history of the continental multi-sport event — capping a remarkable weekend in which India beat Pakistan in both clashes and carried home gold medals in each sport.

Back-to-back classics within 24 hours

The two encounters took place within roughly a day of each other. On Thursday, the hockey semifinal at Kakamigahara produced a thriller: India raced to a 3-0 lead through two goals from captain Harmanpreet Singh and one from Sukhjeet Singh, only for Pakistan to level at 3-3 through Abu Mahmood, Hannan Shahid and Waheed Rana. With a shootout looming, Abhishek struck the winner in the final minute, his effort deflecting off Sufyan Khan and wrong-footing the Pakistan goalkeeper for a 4-3 win.

https://x.com/TheHockeyIndia/status/2106358970193678832

The next day, the cricket final delivered its own drama. Sent in to bat, India posted 211 for 6, powered by Abhishek Sharma's 61 off barely 20 balls and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51, with Shivam Dube adding late muscle in a 62-run stand in the final five overs. Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi announced himself with back-to-back sixes in the second over before falling for 15. Pakistan's chase was kept alive by Hasan Nawaz's 96 off 51 balls, but after Washington Sundar removed Abdul Samad and Jasprit Bumrah conceded only 11 in the penultimate over, Pakistan finished on 192 for 6 — 19 runs short.

What the OCA announced

"The broadcast had the biggest viewership ever for the Games. Thanks to two big matches: yesterday, the Pakistan-India cricket match was the most-viewed match, and the day before, on Thursday, the Pakistan-India hockey match was the most-viewed match ever in the Games' history."

— Tayyab Ikram, President, OCA Coordination Committee

OCA Coordination Committee president Tayyab Ikram made the announcement at a Sunday press conference but disclosed no audience figures and did not specify which match drew the larger crowd. He also pointed to the Games' sporting scale: 212 Asian Games records were broken in Aichi-Nagoya, alongside 54 world records, 89 Asian records and 11 junior world records, which OCA Director General Husain Al-Musallam credited to "the best environment the organising committee created for the athletes."

Ikram acknowledged criticism over logistics, including the cost-cutting decision to house 17,000 athletes and officials in hotels, temporary wooden containers and a cruise ship instead of a traditional Athletes' Village. "Of course there were some challenges, but the way we handled the challenges should be more important to highlight," he said.

Why this rivalry moves the needle

India and Pakistan meet only in international tournaments on neutral ground because of political tensions between the two countries, which gives every encounter an intensity few sporting rivalries can match. In cricket, the win extended India's recent dominance in the shortest format — India's seventh consecutive T20I victory over Pakistan, according to ESPN, following a 61-run win in February 2026. The ICC confirmed the final medal standings: India gold, Pakistan silver, Sri Lanka bronze.

In hockey, the stakes were arguably higher: India were the defending champions and needed the semifinal victory to keep their bid for direct qualification to the LA 2028 Olympics alive.

A golden fortnight for India

India made the most of both wins. The hockey team recovered from the late scare to beat Malaysia 5-1 in the final and defend its Asian Games title. The cricket team closed out the tournament on top of the podium for its second consecutive Asian Games gold after Hangzhou 2023, while the women's team retained its title — a rare treble of team-sport golds at a single Games.

What's next

Detailed broadcast figures are expected in the coming days, which will settle whether the cricket final or the hockey semifinal drew the bigger audience. For India's hockey team, attention now turns to consolidating its place at LA 2028, while cricket's young core — Sharma, Varma and the 15-year-old Sooryavanshi — has given selectors a glimpse of the squad's future.
image_caption: Two Indian hockey players celebrate during a match at the FIH Hockey World Cup in 2026. India beat Pakistan 4-3 in the Asian Games hockey semifinal at Aichi-Nagoya, one of two India-Pakistan clashes the Olympic Council of Asia called the most-viewed in the event’s history.
nri_angle: Indian diaspora audiences from New Jersey to Dubai form a large share of the global viewership for India-Pakistan fixtures, making this weekend's double-header and record audience a shared cultural moment.
